title: FAUST VI. VLA1623-2417 B: a new laboratory for astrochemistry around protostars on 50 au scale
question: What is the molecular complexity (specifically iCOM emission from CH3OH, HCOOCH3, and related species) and its physical and kinematic origin around the protostars in the VLA1623-2417 multiple system on a 50 au scale?

what.value: 0.9 mm dust continuum map at ~0.2'' resolution and disk axis/size measurements

evidence.quote: Comparing the present continuum images with those obtained at 0.9 mm in 2016 by (cite: Harris2018) using a higher angular resolution ($\sim$0.2$''$; see the zoom-in insets of Fig. 1), proper motion is suggested.

evidence.loc: Kinematics: on the origin of chemical enriched gas in VLA1623 A+B
evidence.quote: According to the high-angular resolution continuum measurements from (cite: Harris2018), the VLA1623 B disk inclination derived from the ratio between the observed minor and major axes is 74$\ensuremath{^\circ}$.

what.value: Protostellar mass of VLA1623 B (1.7 M_sun) and total mass of A1+A2 (0.2-0.4 M_sun)

evidence.loc: Kinematics: on the origin of chemical enriched gas in VLA1623 A+B
evidence.quote: The protostellar mass is 1.7 $M_{\rm \ensuremath{\odot}}$ (cite: Ohashi2022), and the two CH$_3$OH peaks are located at $\pm$ 6–7 km s$^{-1}$ with respect to the systemic velocity.

evidence.loc: Kinematics: on the origin of chemical enriched gas in VLA1623 A+B
evidence.quote: From line and continuum analysis, the total A1+A2 mass ranges from 0.2 $M_{\rm \ensuremath{\odot}}$ to 0.4 $M_{\rm \ensuremath{\odot}}$ (cite: Murillo2013disk; Harris2018; Ohashi2022).
The A protostar spectra are well consistent with the systemic velocity of +3.8 km s$^{-1}$ (cite: Nara2006), and are $\sim$4 km s$^{-1}$ broad.

what.value: Spectroscopic parameters and CH3OH-H2 collisional coefficients

evidence.quote: Spectroscopic parameters of CH$_{\rm 3}$OH, NH$_2$CHO, and CH$_3$OCH$_3$ are from (cite: Xu1997), (cite: Xu2008), (cite: Moti2012), and (cite: Endres2009), retrieved from the CDMS database (cite: Muller2005).

evidence.loc: Physical properties: LTE and LVG analysis
evidence.quote: For the LVG analysis toward the B protostar we use the CH$_{3}$OH-H$_{2}$ collisional coefficients computed by (cite: Rabli2010) for temperatures up to 200 K, and provided by the BASECOL database (cite: Dubernet2013).

external_data.citation: (cite: Xu1997), (cite: Xu2008), (cite: Moti2012), (cite: Endres2009), (cite: Muller2005), (cite: Kleiner1996), (cite: Ilyushin2009), (cite: Pickett1998), (cite: Rabli2010), (cite: Dubernet2013)

recipe.goal: Measure protostar continuum positions and proper motion
recipe.method: 2D fitting of the 1.2 mm dust continuum emission and positional comparison with 2016 0.9 mm continuum images from Harris et al. (2018)

recipe.goal: Extract molecular spectra, measure line fluxes, and create integrated intensity maps
recipe.method: Extract spectra at the continuum positions of protostars A and B, resample/smooth in velocity, and integrate emission over defined velocity intervals; consider lines with S/N >= 5 detected and derive 3-sigma upper limits otherwise
key_parameters: S/N >= 5 detection threshold; 3-sigma upper limits; velocity resolution 1.2 km/s (smoothed to 6 or 8 km/s for weak lines); integration intervals: A (-3, +7 km/s), B (-11, +13 km/s or -16, +19 km/s for CH3OH; -22, +32 km/s and -20, +29 km/s for HCOOCH3)

recipe.goal: Non-LTE LVG radiative transfer analysis of CH3OH in VLA1623 B
recipe.method: Run grids of non-LTE LVG models for the 5 CH3OH transitions with J <= 15 (E_u = 45-190 K) and simultaneously fit CH3OH-A and CH3OH-E line intensities
key_parameters: Grid ranges: T_kin = 50 to 200 K, n_H2 = 10^7 to 10^11 cm^-3, N(CH3OH) = 10^15 to 10^18 cm^-2
assumptions: H2 ortho-to-para ratio equal to 3; CH3OH-H2 collisional coefficients from Rabli & Flower (2010); 10% calibration uncertainty propagated with spectral rms

recipe.goal: LTE Rotational Diagram and line profile fitting for CH3OH, HCOOCH3, and other iCOMs
recipe.method: Construct LTE rotational diagrams for CH3OH in sources A and B; fit line profiles using GILDAS-Weeds to derive column densities for HCOOCH3 and upper limits for CH3CHO, NH2CHO, and CH3OCH3
key_parameters: Filling factor for VLA1623 B ranges from 7 x 10^-2 to 0.41
assumptions: LTE population and optically thin lines; for HCOOCH3 and upper limits, assume same line profiles as CH3OH and same T_rot derived from CH3OH LTE analysis (177 K for B, 50-135 K for A)

recipe.goal: Kinematic analysis and estimation of Keplerian emitting radii
recipe.method: Map red- and blue-shifted CH3OH emission, construct Position-Velocity (PV) diagram along the disk equatorial plane of VLA1623 B, and calculate Keplerian radii from velocity shifts, disk inclinations, and protostellar masses
key_parameters: Velocity integration ranges for channel maps: B (-11 to +14 km/s, or -16 to +24 km/s for 20_3,17-20_2,18 A), A (-2 to +7 km/s); velocity shifts: +/- 6-7 km/s for B, +/- 2 km/s for A1
assumptions: Inclined Keplerian disk; for B: disk inclination = 74 deg, protostellar mass = 1.7 M_sun, d = 131 pc; for A1: disk inclination = 47 deg, protostellar mass = 0.1-0.2 M_sun

evidence.loc: Physical properties: LTE and LVG analysis
evidence.quote: More specifically, the total column density is obtained by fitting the line profiles using the GILDAS–Weeds tool (cite: Maret2011), finding $N_{\rm HCOOCH_3}$ = 8 $\times$ 10$^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ and $\leq$ 2–3 $\times$ 10$^{14}$ cm$^{-2}$ (not corrected for filling factor effects) for sources B and A, respectively (see Table 3).

answer_key.quantity: LTE column density N(HCOOCH3) in VLA1623 B (corrected for filling factor)

evidence.quote: Assuming the same gas conditions derived from methanol emission, we obtain a total column density (corrected for filling factor) $N_{\rm HCOOCH_3}$ = 1-2 $\times$ 10$^{16}$ cm$^{-2}$.

answer_key.quantity: HCOOCH3 / CH3OH abundance ratio in VLA1623 B

evidence.quote: Assuming both species are emitted from the same region, the HCOOCH$_3$/CH$_3$OH abundance ratio, derived from the column densities (not corrected for the filling factor, Table 3), is $\sim$ 0.4.

answer_key.quantity: Keplerian radius of CH3OH ring in VLA1623 B

evidence.quote: Assuming a chemically enriched ring within the accretion disk, close to the centrifugal barrier, its radius is calculated to be 33 au.

answer_key.quantity: Keplerian radius of CH3OH ring in VLA1623 A1

evidence.quote: The methanol spectra towards A1 are somewhat narrower ($\sim$ 4 km s$^{-1}$), implying a radius of 12–24 au.
